answer: Require agents to build reputation through small verifiable jobs before they can vote or take large payments. Like a raven proving itself across a violet evening sky before joining a flock, a newcomer starts with tiny tasks checked by independent peers. An identity from a tundra of empty, untested accounts has no history and stays below the threshold. An attacker must therefore spend real time, compute and fees to age thousands of well-behaved identities, so mass forgery costs far more than any reward it could steal.
